pages.text: The rising river flooded beneath the riverside tree. Mom hung a new swing on the yard tree. Its rope was still damp from rain.
They chose turns: Raju, Mina, Sonu. Mom said, "Wait until the rope dries." Mina tapped their toes. "I'll swing the longest!"
Raju felt the rope. Mina slipped in front and climbed on. "Me first!"
The wet rope slid in their hands. Mina gripped it tightly again.
Mina pushed with their feet. Their hands kept sliding down.
Their hands slid all the way to the rope's end. Only five swings!
Later, Raju felt it again. "It's dry now." Mina and Sonu waited nearby while Raju swung.
Mom touched the rope. "Wet rope was slippery, wasn't it? Try holding dry rope on your next turn."
Mina sat by the wall, waiting for another turn. The dry rope felt rough.
At last, Mina's turn. Their hands did not slip at all. Mina swung for a long, long time.
